description: 5 VLANs (Student/Faculty/Admin/Server/Guest) isolate broadcast domains so a device in one zone cannot see or sniff traffic from another zone, even on the same trunk backbone (proven in Attack #1)

Extended ACLs on Router0's sub-interfaces block Student/Guest from Admin+Server and limit Faculty to App-Server only, stopping unauthorized cross-VLAN access (Attack #2) and a targeted ICMP flood (Attack #3)
Shuts the port down the instant an unregistered MAC appears on an access port (rogue device, Attack #4), preserving access-layer integrity and generating a syslog record for accountability
Encrypted remote management (SSH only, Telnet disabled) on Router0 and all 5 switches prevents credential sniffing and logs who configured each device
All 5 switches + Router0 forward security events (ACL denies, port-security violations, config changes) to one Syslog-Server, giving a single source of truth for detection and audit
